questions.text: Consider a system with the transfer function [latex]G(s)=\frac{s+6}{ks^{2}+s+6}[/latex]. Its damping ratio will be 0.5 when the value of k is
questions.solution: [latex]\begin{array}{l} \frac{s+6}{k\left(s^{2}+\frac{s}{k}+\frac{6}{k}\right)} \\ \text { Comparing with } s^{2}+2 \xi \omega_{n}+\omega_{n}^{2} \\ \begin{aligned} \omega_{n}&=\sqrt{\frac{6}{k}} \\ 2 \xi \omega_{n}&=\frac{1}{k} \\ 2 \times 0.5 \times \sqrt{\frac{6}{k}}&=\frac{1}{k} \\ \Rightarrow \qquad \frac{6}{k}&=\frac{1}{k^{2}} \\ k&=\frac{1}{6} \end{aligned} \end{array}[/latex]

questions.text: The open-loop DC gain of a unity negative feedback system with closed-loop transfer function [latex]\frac{s+4}{s^{2}+7s+13}[/latex] is
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \mathrm{CLTF} &=\frac{G(s)}{1+G(s) H(s)}=\frac{s+4}{s^{2}+7 s+13} \\ \frac{1+G(s) H(s)}{G(s)} &=\frac{s^{2}+7 s+13}{s+4} \end{aligned} [/latex]
[latex] H(s)=1[/latex] for unity feedback.
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{1}{G(s)} &=\frac{s^{2}+7 s+13}{s+4}-1 \\ \frac{1}{G(s)} &=\frac{s^{2}+6 s+9}{s+4} \\ \therefore \quad G(s) &=\frac{s+4}{s^{2}+6 s+9} \\ \text { For D.C. } \quad s&=0\\ \therefore \quad G(s) &=\text{open loop gain} \\ &=\frac{4}{9} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: If the characteristic equation of a closed-loop system is [latex]s^{2}+2s+2=0[/latex], then the system is
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} s^{2}+2 \xi \omega_{n}+\omega_{n}^{2} &=0 \\ 2 \xi\omega{n} &=2, \xi=\frac{1}{\omega_{n}} \\ \omega_{n} &=\sqrt{2}\\ \therefore \quad \xi&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] \because \xi \lt 1,[/latex] hence response will be underdamped.

questions.text:
Consider the unity negative feedback control system shown in the Figure.
The value of gain [latex]K (>0)[/latex] at which the given system will remain marginally stable is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.solution:
Given:
Open-loop: [latex]\frac{K}{s(s+7)(s+11)}[/latex], unity negative feedback.

Step 1: Characteristic equation

[latex] s(s+7)(s+11) + K = 0 [/latex]
[latex] s^3 + 18s^2 + 77s + K = 0 [/latex]

Step 2: Routh-Hurwitz array

[latex] \begin{array}{c|cc} s^3 & 1 & 77 \ s^2 & 18 & K \ s^1 & \frac{18\times77 - K}{18} & 0 \ s^0 & K & \end{array} [/latex]

Step 3: Marginal stability - [latex]s^1[/latex] row = 0

[latex] \frac{18\times77 - K}{18} = 0 [/latex]
[latex] K = 18\times77 = 1386 [/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the polynomial

[latex]p(s)=s^{5}+7 s^{4}+3 s^{3}-33 s^{2}+2 s-40[/latex].

Let [latex](L,I,R)[/latex] be defined as follows.
[latex]L[/latex] is the number of roots of [latex]p(s)[/latex] with negative real parts.
[latex]I[/latex] is the number of roots of [latex]\mathrm{p}(\mathrm{s})[/latex] that are purely imaginary.
[latex]R[/latex] is the number of roots of [latex]p(s)[/latex] with positive real parts.

Which one of the following options is correct?
questions.solution:
Given [latex]p(s)=s^{5}+7 s^{4}+3 s^{3}-33 s^{2}+2 s-40[/latex]
[latex] \begin{array}{l|lrl} s^{5} & 1 & 3 & 2 \\ s^{4} & 7 & -33 & -40 \\ s^{3} & \frac{54}{7} & \frac{54}{7} & 0 \\ s^{2} & -40 & -40 & 0 \\ s^{1} & 0(-80) & 0 & 0 \\ s^{0} & -40 & & \\ \end{array} [/latex]
Auxiliary equation [A.E] [latex]-40 \mathrm{~s}^{2}-40=0[/latex]
A.E [latex]\Rightarrow \mathrm{s}^{2}+1=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{~s}^{2}=-1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{~s}= \pm 1 \mathrm{j}[/latex]
So number of imaginary roots [latex][\mathrm{I}]=2[/latex]

questions.text:
In the feedback control system shown in the figure below [latex]G(s)=\frac{6}{s(s+1)(s+2)}[/latex].

[latex]R(s), Y(s)[/latex], and [latex]E(s)[/latex] are the Laplace transforms of [latex]r(t), y(t)[/latex], and [latex]e(t)[/latex], respectively. If the input [latex]r(t)[/latex] is a unit step function, then _____
options: [latex]\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} e(t)[/latex] does not exist, [latex]e(t)[/latex] is oscillatory
questions.solution:
Given system is


[latex] G(s)=\frac{6}{s(s+1)(s+2)} [/latex]
The characteristic equation,
[latex] \begin{aligned} 1+G(s) & =0 \\ 1+\frac{6}{s(s+1)(s+2)} & =0 \\ s(s+1)(s+2)+6 & =0 \\ s^{3}+3 s^{2}+2 s+6 & =0 \end{aligned} [/latex]
Clearly, here the internal coefficient product is equal to external coefficient product i.e.,
[latex] 3 \times 2=6 \times 1 [/latex]
Hence, the given system is marginally stable system.
[latex]\therefore e(t)[/latex] not exist because system is oscillatory system.

questions.text: The characteristic equation of an LTI system is given by [latex]F(s)=s^{5}+2s^{4}+3s^{3}+6s^{2}-4s-8=0[/latex] The number of roots that lie strictly in the left half s-plane is _________.
questions.solution:
Using Routh's tabular or:
[latex] \begin{array}{c|lll} s^{5} & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ s^{4} & 2 & 6 & -8 \\ s^{3} & 0 8 & 0(12) & 0 \\ s^{2} & 3 & -8 & 0 \\ s^{1} & \frac{100}{3} & 0 & 0 \\ s^{0} & -8 & & \end{array}[/latex]
Auxiliary equation:
[latex] \begin{aligned} A &=2 s^{4}+6 s^{2}-8=0 \\ \frac{d A}{d s} &=8 s^{3}+12 s=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
As one time row of zero occur in Routh's table therefore a pair of imaginary pole exists, also number of sign change in Routh's table is one. Hence, two poles lie strictly in the left half of s-plane.

questions.text: A plant transfer function is given as [latex]G(s)=(K_{P}+\frac{K_{I}}{s})\frac{1}{s(s+2)}[/latex]. When the plant operates in a unity feedback configuration, the condition for the stability of the closed loop system is
questions.solution:
[latex]G(s)=\left(K_{p}+\frac{K_{I}}{s}\right)\left(\frac{1}{s(s+2)}\right)[/latex]
The closed loop transfer function for unity feedback
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{G(s)}{1+G(s)} &=\frac{\left(K_{p} s+K_{I}\right)}{s^{2}(s+2)+\left(K_{p} s+K_{I}\right)} \\ &=\frac{K_{p} s+K_{I}}{s^{3}+2 s^{2}+K_{p} s+K_{I}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Using Routh's tabular form:
[latex] \begin{array}{c|cc} s^{3} & 1 & K_{p} \\ s^{2} & 2 & K_{I} \\ s^{1} & \frac{2 K_{p}-K_{I}}{2} & 0 \\ s^{0} & K_{p} & \end{array}[/latex]
For system to be stable;
[latex] \begin{aligned} K_{p}& \gt 0\\ \text{and }\frac{2 K_{p}-K_{I}}{2}& \gt 0 \\ \text{or} \quad 2 K_{p}-K_{I}& \gt 0 \\ \text{or} \quad K_{p}& \gt \frac{K_{I}}{2} \gt 0 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: Consider a transfer function [latex]G_{p}(s)=\frac{ps^{2}+3ps-2}{s^{2}+(3+p)s+(2-p)}[/latex] with [latex]p[/latex] a positive real parameter. The maximum value of [latex]p[/latex] until which [latex]G_{p}[/latex] remains stable is ____.
questions.solution:
Given transfer function
[latex] G_{p}(s)=\frac{p s^{2}+3 p s-2}{s^{2}+(3+p) s+(2-p)} \qquad\ldots(i)[/latex]
The characteristic equation is
[latex] =s^{2}+(3+p) s+(2-p)\qquad\ldots(ii)[/latex]
Using Routh Hurtwiz criterion,
[latex] \begin{array}{l|ll} s^{2} & 1 & (2-P) \\ s^{1} & (3+p) & 0 \\ s^{0} & (2-p) & 0 \end{array}[/latex]
For system to be remain stable
[latex] \begin{aligned} 2-p & \geq 0 \\ p_{\max } &=1.99 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text:
The forward path transfer function of a unity negative feedback system is given by
[latex]G(s)=\frac{K}{(s+2)(s-1)}[/latex]
The value of K which will place both the poles of the closed-loop system at the same location, is ______.
questions.solution:
Given that, [latex]\quad G(s)=\frac{K}{(s+2)(s-1)} [/latex]
Using root locus method, the break point can be obtain as


[latex] \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad 1+G(s)&=0 \\ 1+\frac{K}{(s+2)(s-1)} &=0 \\ \text{or }\quad K&=-(s+2)(s-1)\\ \frac{d K}{d s} &=-2 s-1=0 \\ \text{or }\quad s &=-0.5 \end{aligned}[/latex]
To have, both the poles at the same directions
[latex] \begin{aligned} |G(s)|_{s=0.5} &=1 \\ K &=2.25 \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex] \begin{aligned} a s^{2}+(1+K)&=0 \\ -a \omega^{2}+(1+K)&=0 \\ \text{given }\quad \omega&=2 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec} \\ -4 a+(1+K)&=0 \\ -4 \frac{(1+K)}{(2+K)}+(1+K)&=0 \\ -4(1+K)+(2+K)(1+K)&=0 \\ (1+K)[(2+K)-4]&=0 \\ K=-1,2 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text:
For the control system shown in the Figure, the transfer function of a plant,
[latex]G(s) = \frac{1}{(s+1)(s+2)}[/latex] is connected in cascade with a compensator
[latex]C(s) = K(s + \alpha)[/latex], where [latex]K[/latex] and [latex]\alpha[/latex] are positive real valued constants.

Which of the following pairs [latex](K, \alpha)[/latex] represent the correct values for the closed loop system to have poles at [latex](-3 \pm j\sqrt{5})[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Given:
Plant: [latex]G(s) = \dfrac{1}{(s+1)(s+2)}[/latex]
Compensator: [latex]C(s) = K(s + \alpha)[/latex]
Desired closed-loop poles: [latex]s = -3 \pm j\sqrt{5}[/latex]

Step 1: Open-loop transfer function

[latex] L(s) = C(s)G(s) = \frac{K(s+\alpha)}{(s+1)(s+2)} [/latex]

Characteristic equation (unity feedback):
[latex] 1 + L(s) = 0 \Rightarrow (s+1)(s+2) + K(s+\alpha) = 0 [/latex]

Step 2: Expand and match with desired polynomial

Desired poles: [latex]s = -3 \pm j\sqrt{5}[/latex]
Desired characteristic polynomial:
[latex] (s+3-j\sqrt{5})(s+3+j\sqrt{5}) = (s+3)^2 + 5 = s^2 + 6s + 14 [/latex]

Expanding the characteristic equation:
[latex] s^2 + 3s + 2 + Ks + K\alpha = 0 [/latex] [latex] s^2 + (3+K)s + (2+K\alpha) = 0 [/latex]

Step 3: Equate coefficients

[latex] 3 + K = 6 \Rightarrow K = 3 [/latex]
[latex] 2 + K\alpha = 14 \Rightarrow 2 + 3\alpha = 14 \Rightarrow \alpha = 4 [/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the unity-negative-feedback system shown in Figure (i) below, where gain [latex]K \geq 0[/latex]. The root locus of this system is shown in Figure (ii) below.

questions.solution:
We are given the root locus plot in Figure (ii), and we are to determine whether a closed-loop pole lies at the complex location [latex] -1 + j1 [/latex] for any [latex] K \geq 0 [/latex].

From control theory, the root locus shows the trajectory of the closed-loop poles as [latex] K [/latex] varies from [latex] 0 [/latex] to [latex] \infty [/latex].

We inspect the root locus diagram in Figure (ii):
The root locus branches are symmetric about the real axis.
The point [latex] -1 + j1 [/latex] lies outside the plotted root locus path.
It is not marked or touched by any of the root locus branches.

Hence, the closed-loop poles never pass through the point [latex] -1 + j1 [/latex] for any positive value of [latex] K [/latex].

questions.text:
The forward-path transfer function and the feedback-path transfer function of a single loop negative feedback control system are given as

[latex]G(s)=\frac{K(s+2)}{s^{2}+2s+2}[/latex] and H(s)=1,

respectively. If the variable parameter K is real positive, then the location of the breakaway point on the root locus diagram of the system is __________
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} G(s) &=\frac{K(s+2)}{s^{2}+2 s+2} \\ H(s)&=1 \\ 1+G(s) H(s) &=0 \\ 1+\frac{K}{\left(s^{2}\right)+2 s+2}(s+2) &=0\\ K&=-\frac{\left(s^{2}+2 s+2\right)}{(s+2)} \end{aligned}[/latex]


[latex] \frac{d K}{d s}=-\left(\frac{(2 s+2)(s+2)-\left(s^{2}+2 s+2\right)}{(s+2)^{2}}\right) [/latex]
For break away points, [latex] \frac{d K}{d s}=0 [/latex]
[latex] \begin{array}{l} (2 s+2)(s+2)-\left(s^{2}+2 s+2\right)=0 \\ 2 s^{2}+6 s+4-s^{2}-2 s-2=0 \\ s^{2}+4 s+2=0 \end{array} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} s&=\frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{16-8}}{2} \\ &=\frac{-4 \pm 2 \sqrt{2}}{2}=-2 \pm \sqrt{2} \\ s&=-0.58 ; s=-3.41 \\ \text{But,}\quad s&=-3.41 \text{ lies on root locus }\\ \text{Hence}\quad s&=-3.41 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text:
The open-loop transfer function of a unity-feedback control system is
[latex]G(s)=\frac{K}{s^{2}+5s+5}[/latex]
The value of K at the breakaway point of the feedback control system's root-locus plot is ________
questions.solution:
Characteristic equation [latex]1+G(s)H(s)=0[/latex]
[latex]1+\frac{K}{s^2+5s+5}=0[/latex]
[latex]K=-s^2-5s-5[/latex]
For break away point [latex]\frac{dK}{ds}=0[/latex]
[latex]\frac{dK}{ds}=-2s+5=0\;\Rightarrow \; s=-2.5[/latex]
According to magnitude condition,
[latex]\begin{aligned} |G(s)H(s)|_{s=-2.5} &=1 \\ |G(s)H(s)|_{s=-2.5} &=\frac{|K|}{|(2.5)^2 +5 \times -2.5+5|}=1 \\ |K|&=|(6.25+5-12.5)|=1.25 \\ K&=\pm 1.25 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: For the system shown in the figure, s = -2.75 lies on the root locus if K is _______.

In order to lie a point s=-2.75, the angle condition must be satisfy and therefore the magnitude condition is
[latex] \begin{aligned} &\mid G(s) H(s) \|_{s=-275}=1 \\ &=\left.\frac{10 K \sqrt{s^{2}+3^{2}}}{\sqrt{s^{2}+2^{2}}}\right|_{s=-2.75}=1 \\ &=\frac{10 K \sqrt{(3-2.75)^{2}}}{\sqrt{(2-2.75)^{2}}}=1 \\ &=\frac{0.25 \times 10 K}{0.75} or K=0.3 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: The open-loop transfer function of a plant in a unity feedback configuration is given as [latex]G(s)=\frac{K(s+4)}{(s+8)(s^{2}-9)}[/latex] . The value of the gain K(> 0) for which -1+ j2 lies on the root locus is_______.
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} G(s) &=\frac{K(s+4)}{(s+8)\left(s^{2}-9\right)} \\ &=\frac{K(s+4)}{(s+8)(s+3)(s-3)} \end{aligned}[/latex]
For the point (-1+2 j) to lie on the root locus the angle condition must be satisfy
i.e. [latex]\angle G(s) H(s)=\pm(2 Q+1) 180^{\circ} [/latex]
Taking LHS:
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \left.\angle G(s) H(s)\right|_{s=-1+2 j} \\ =\frac{\angle K+\angle(s+4)}{\angle(s+8)+\angle(s+3)+\angle(s-3)} \\ =\frac{\angle K+\angle(-1+2 j+4)}{\angle(-1+2 j+8)+\angle(-1+2 j+3)+\angle(-1+2 j-3)} \\ =\frac{0+\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)}{\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{7}\right)+\tan ^{-1}(1)+180^{\circ}-\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)} \\ =33.69^{\circ}-15.945^{\circ}-45^{\circ}-180^{\circ}+26.565^{\circ} \\ \simeq 180^{\circ} \end{array}[/latex]
As angle condition is satisfied the value of system gain K can be obtained by using magnitude
condition
[latex] \begin{array}{l} i.e. |G(s) H(s)|_{s=-1+2 j}=1 \\ =\frac{K \sqrt{(-1+4)^{2}+2^{2}}}{\sqrt{(-1+8)^{2}+2^{2}} \cdot \sqrt{(-1+3)^{2}+2^{2}} \cdot \sqrt{(-1-3)^{2}+2^{2}}} \\ =1 \\ =\frac{K \sqrt{9+4}}{\sqrt{49+4} \sqrt{4+4} \sqrt{16+4}}=1 \\ =\frac{K \sqrt{13}}{\sqrt{53} \sqrt{8} \sqrt{20}}=1 \\ K=\frac{\sqrt{53 \times 8 \times 20}}{\sqrt{13}}=25.54 \end{array}[/latex]

questions.solution:
[latex]G(s)=\frac{K}{s(s+1)(s+3)}[/latex]
The characteristic equation
[latex] \begin{array}{l} =1+G(s) H(s)=0 \\ =s(s+1)(s+3)+K=0 \\ =s^{3}+4 s^{2}+3 s+K=0 \end{array}[/latex]
Using Routh's tabular form
[latex] \begin{array}{c|cc} s^{3} & 1 & 3 \\ s^{2} & 4 & K \\ s^{1} & \frac{12-K}{4} & 0 \\ s^{0} & K & \end{array}[/latex]
In order to cross the imaginary axis, system
should be marginally stable
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{12-K}{4}&=0\\ \text{or }\quad K&=12 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text:
The Nyquist plot of a system is given in the figure. Let [latex] \omega_P, \omega_Q, \omega_R [/latex] and [latex] \omega_S [/latex] be the positive frequencies at the points [latex]P, Q, R,[/latex] and [latex]S,[/latex] respectively.
Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
options: [latex] \omega_S [/latex] is the gain crossover frequency and [latex] \omega_P [/latex] is the phase crossover frequency
[latex] \omega_Q [/latex] is the gain crossover frequency and [latex] \omega_S [/latex] is the phase crossover frequency
[latex] \omega_R [/latex] is the gain crossover frequency and [latex] \omega_S [/latex] is the phase crossover frequency
[latex] \omega_S [/latex] is the gain crossover frequency and [latex] \omega_Q [/latex] is the phase crossover frequency
questions.solution:
From the Nyquist plot:
The gain crossover frequency is the frequency at which the Nyquist plot crosses the unit circle, i.e., the magnitude of the open-loop transfer function [latex] |G(j\omega)H(j\omega)| = 1 [/latex].
The phase crossover frequency is the frequency at which the phase is [latex] -180^\circ [/latex], i.e., the Nyquist plot crosses the negative real axis.

From the diagram:
Point S lies on the unit circle, so [latex] \omega_S [/latex] is the gain crossover frequency.
Point P lies on the negative real axis, hence [latex] \omega_P [/latex] is the phase crossover frequency.

Therefore, the correct statement is: [latex] \omega_S [/latex] is the gain crossover frequency and [latex] \omega_P [/latex] is the phase crossover frequency.

questions.text:
For a unity feedback control system with the forward path transfer function

[latex]G(s)=\frac{K}{s(s+2)}[/latex]

The peak resonant magnitude [latex]M_{r}[/latex], of the closed-loop frequency response is 2. The corresponding value of the gain K (correct to two decimal places) is _________.
questions.solution:
Maximum resonant peak,
[latex]\begin{aligned} M_{r} &=\frac{1}{2 \xi \sqrt{1-\xi^{2}}}=2 \\ 2 \xi \sqrt{1-\xi^{2}} &=\frac{1}{2} \\ \xi^{2}\left(1-\xi^{2}\right) &=\frac{1}{16} \\ \xi^{4}-\xi^{2}+\frac{1}{16} &=0 \\ \xi^{2}&=\frac{1}{2} \pm \sqrt{\frac{1-\frac{1}{4}}{4}}=\frac{1}{2} \pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \\ \text { As } M_{r}=2 \gt 1, \xi& \lt \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \text { and } \xi^{2} \lt \frac{1}{2} \\ \text { So. } \quad\xi^{2}&=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\\ Given, \quad G(s)&=\frac{K}{s(s+2)}=\frac{\omega_{n}^{2}}{s\left(s+2 \xi \omega_{n}\right)} \\ \text{So} \quad\omega_{n} &=\sqrt{K} \\ 2 \xi \sqrt{K} &=2\\ \sqrt{K} &=\frac{1}{\xi} \\ K &=\frac{1}{\xi^{2}}=\frac{1}{\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right)} \\ &=\frac{4}{2-\sqrt{3}}=14.928 \end{aligned}[/latex]

So,
[latex] P=2[/latex]

questions.text:

[latex]G(s)=\frac{(s^{2}+9)(s+2)}{(s+1)(s+3)(s+4)}[/latex]
is excited by sin([latex]\omega[/latex] t). The steady-state output of the system is zero at
questions.solution:
Transfer function is
[latex] \begin{aligned} G(s)&=\frac{\left(s^{2}+9\right)(s+2)}{(s+1)(s+3)(s+4)} \\ \text{Input }\quad X(s)&=L \cdot T[\sin \omega t]\\ X(s)&=\frac{\omega}{s^{2}+\omega^{2}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
So output
[latex] Y(s)=\frac{\left(s^{2}+9\right)(s+2)}{(s+1)(s+3)(s+4)} \cdot \frac{\omega}{\left(s^{2}+\omega^{2}\right)}[/latex]
Now
[latex] \lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} y(t)=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} S Y(s)=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} s \frac{\left(s^{2}+9\right)(s+2)}{(s+1)(s+3)(s+4)} \cdot \frac{\omega}{\left(s^{2}+\omega^{2}\right)}[/latex]
this will be zero if [latex] s^{2}+\omega^{2}[/latex] will cancel [latex]\left(s^{2}+9\right)[/latex] term as only then final value theorem will be applicable.
So at [latex]\omega^{2}=9 \Rightarrow \omega=3 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec},[/latex] steady state output will be zero.

questions.text:
The state and output equations for a control system are:

[latex]\dot{x} = \begin{bmatrix} -4 & -1.5 \\ 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix} x + \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} u[/latex]; [latex]y = \begin{bmatrix} 1.5 & 0.625 \end{bmatrix} x[/latex]

Which of the following expressions correctly represents the transfer function [latex]\frac{Y(s)}{U(s)}[/latex] of the system with zero initial conditions?
questions.solution:
Given:
[latex] \dot{x} = \begin{bmatrix} -4 & -1.5 \\ 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix} x + \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} u [/latex]
[latex] y = \begin{bmatrix} 1.5 & 0.625 \end{bmatrix} x [/latex]

Step 1: Transfer function formula

[latex] \frac{Y(s)}{U(s)} = C(sI - A)^{-1}B [/latex]

Step 2: Compute (sI - A)

[latex] sI - A = \begin{bmatrix} s+4 & 1.5 \\ -4 & s \end{bmatrix} [/latex]

Step 3: Determinant

[latex] \det(sI-A) = s(s+4) + 6 = s^2 + 4s + 6 [/latex]

Step 4: Inverse of (sI - A)

[latex] (sI-A)^{-1} = \frac{1}{s^2+4s+6}\begin{bmatrix} s & -1.5 \\ 4 & s+4 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]

Step 5: Multiply [latex] C(sI-A)^{-1} B [/latex]

[latex] (sI-A)^{-1}B = \frac{1}{s^2+4s+6}\begin{bmatrix} s & -1.5 \\ 4 & s+4 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2\\0\end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{s^2+4s+6}\begin{bmatrix}2s\\8\end{bmatrix} [/latex]

[latex] \frac{Y(s)}{U(s)} = \begin{bmatrix}1.5 & 0.625\end{bmatrix}\frac{1}{s^2+4s+6}\begin{bmatrix}2s\\8\end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex] = \frac{1}{s^2+4s+6}\left(1.5 \times 2s + 0.625 \times 8\right) [/latex]
[latex] = \frac{3s + 5}{s^2 + 4s + 6} [/latex]

questions.text:
A satellite attitude control system, as shown below, has a plant with transfer function [latex]G(s)=\frac{1}{s^{2}}[/latex] cascaded with a compensator [latex]C(s)=\frac{K(s+\alpha)}{s+4}[/latex], where [latex]K[/latex] and [latex]\alpha[/latex] are positive real constants.

In order for the closed-loop system to have poles at [latex]-1 \pm j \sqrt{3}[/latex], the value of [latex]\alpha[/latex] must be ____
questions.solution:
[latex] G(S) C(s)=\frac{1}{S^{2}} \frac{k(S+\alpha)}{(S+4)} [/latex]
Characteristic equation is
[latex] S^{3}+4 S^{2}+k S+\alpha=0 [/latex]
Poles of the system present at [latex]=-1 \pm j \sqrt{3}[/latex]
Characteristic equation is
[latex] \begin{aligned} &(S+a)\left[(S+1)^{2}+3\right]=0 \\ &(S+a)\left(S^{2}+2 S+4\right)=0 \\ & S^{3}+(2+a) S^{2}+(4+2 a) S+4 a=0 \end{aligned} [/latex]
Compare equation (I) and (II)
[latex] \begin{aligned} 2+a & =4 \\ a & =2 \\ 4+2 a & =k \\ k & =8 \\ k \alpha & =4 a \\ \alpha & =\frac{8}{8}=1 \\ \alpha & =1 \end{aligned} [/latex]

questions.text:
A unity feedback system that uses proportional-integral ([latex]\text{PI}[/latex] ) control is shown in the figure.

The stability of the overall system is controlled by tuning the [latex]\text{PI}[/latex] control parameters [latex]K_{P}[/latex] and [latex]K_{I}[/latex]. The maximum value of [latex]K_{I}[/latex] that can be chosen so as to keep the overall system stable or, in the worst case, marginally stable (rounded off to three decimal places) is ______
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} G H &=\left(\frac{s K_{p}+K_{I}}{s}\right)\left(\frac{2}{s^{3}+4 s^{2}+5 s+2}\right) \\ q(s) &=s^{4}+4 s^{3}+5 s^{2}+s\left(2+2 k_{p}\right)+2 k_{I} \\ \text{Necessary}:\qquad K_{p} & \gt -1 ; K_{I} \gt 0\\ &\begin{array}{l|ccc} s^{4} & 1 & 5 & 2 K_{I} \\ s^{3} & 4 & 2+2 K_{p} & \\ s^{2} & \frac{18-2 K_{p}}{4} & 2 K_{I} & \\ s^{1} & \left(9-K_{p}\right)\left(1+K_{p}\right)-8 K_{I} & & \\ s^{0} & 2 K_{I} & & \end{array}\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
Sufficient:
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{18-2 K_{p}}{4}& \gt 0\\ \Rightarrow \quad K_{p}& \lt 9\\ \therefore \quad-1& \lt K_{p} \lt 9\\ \left(18-2 K_{p}\right)\left(2+2 K_{p}\right)-32 K_{I}& \gt 0\\ 32 K_{I}& \lt 36+32 K_{p}-4 K_{p}^{2}\\ \therefore \qquad \qquad 0& \lt K_{I} \lt \frac{36+32 K_{p}-4 K_{p}^{2}}{32} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text{If }K_{p}&=-1 \Rightarrow k_{I}=0\\ \text{If }K_{p}&=9 \Rightarrow k_{I}=0\\ \end{aligned}[/latex],
[latex]\begin{aligned} \therefore \qquad \qquad \frac{d K_{I}}{d K_{p}}&=0\\ \Rightarrow \qquad \qquad 32-8 K_{p}&=0=0 \Rightarrow K_{p}=4 \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] \therefore [/latex] For [latex]K_{p}=4, K_{I}[/latex] is maximum, which is
[latex] K_{I}=\frac{36+32 \times 4-64}{32}=3.125[/latex]
For [latex]K_{p}=4, K_{I} \lt 3.125[/latex] for stability
[latex] \therefore K_{I \max }=3.125[/latex]

questions.text: For the following feedback system [latex]G(s)=\frac{1}{(s+1)(s+2)}[/latex]. The 2% settling time of the step response is required to be less than 2 seconds. Which one of the following compensators C(s) achieves this ?

Given open loop transfer function is
[latex] \begin{aligned} G(s)&=\frac{1}{(s+1)(s+2)} \\ \therefore T(s)&=\frac{G(s)}{1+G(s)}=\frac{1}{(s+1)(s+2)+1} \\ T(s)&=\frac{1}{s^{2}+3 s+3} &\ldots(i) \end{aligned}[/latex]
Comparing equation (i) with standard transfer function
[latex] \xi \omega_{n}=\frac{3}{2}=1.5 [/latex]
[latex] \therefore [/latex] 2% settling time
[latex] \tau_{s}=\frac{4}{\xi \omega_{n}}=\frac{4}{1.5}=2.67>2 \mathrm{sec} [/latex]
Thus, in order to make settling time [latex]\left(\tau_{s}\right)[/latex] less than 2 sec, PD controller should be used. Hence, option (C) is the correct choice.
Where, [latex]C(s)=2(s+4) [/latex]
[latex] \therefore [/latex] New transfer function [latex]=T^{\prime}(G)[/latex]
[latex] =\frac{C(s) G(s)}{1+C(s) G(s)}=\frac{2(s+4)}{s^{2}+3 s+2+2 s+8} [/latex]
or [latex]T^{\prime}(s)=\frac{2(s+4)}{s^{2}+5 s+10}[/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad \tau_{s}=\frac{4}{\xi \omega_{n}}=\frac{4}{5 / 2}=\frac{4}{2.5}=1.6[/latex]

questions.text: A unity negative feedback closed loop system has a plant with the transfer function [latex]G(s)=\frac{1}{s^{2}+2s+2}[/latex] and a controller [latex]G_{c}(s)[/latex] in the feed forward path. Steady state error,
[latex] \begin{aligned} e_{s s} &=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} \frac{s R(s)}{1+G(s) G_{c}(s)} \\ r(t) &=u(t) \\ R(s) &=\frac{1}{s} \\ e_{ss} &=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} \frac{s \cdot \frac{1}{s}}{1+G(s) G_{c}(s)} \\ e_{ss}&=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} \frac{1}{1+G(s) G_{c}(s)} \\ \text { Taking, } \quad G_{c}(s) &=\frac{s+1}{s+2}, e_{s s}=\frac{2}{3} \\ \text { Taking, } \quad G_{c}(s) &=\frac{s+2}{s+1}, e_{s s}=\frac{1}{3} \\ \text { Taking, } \quad G_{c}(s) &=\frac{(s+1)(s+4)}{(s+2)(s+3)}, e_{s s}=\frac{3}{5} \\ \text { Taking, } \quad & G_{c}(s)=1+\frac{2}{s}+3 s, e_{s s}=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]

Comparing with standard second order eq.
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \text{i.e.}\quad s^{2}+2 \xi \omega_{n} s+\omega_{n}^{2}=0\\ \text{So,} \quad \omega_{n}=100 ; 2 \xi \omega_{n}=10+100 K_{0} \\ \text{Given,}\quad \xi=0.5 \\ 2 \times 0.5 \times 100=10+100 K_{0} \\ K_{D}=0.9 \end{array}[/latex]

questions.text:
Let the state-space representation of an LTI system be [latex]\dot{x}(t)=Ax(t)+Bu(t)[/latex], [latex]\dot{y}(t)=Cx(t)+du(t)[/latex] where A, B, C are matrices, d is a scalar, u(t) is the input to the system, and y(t) is its output. Let [latex]B=[0\;0\;1]^T[/latex] and d=0. Which one of the following options for A and C will ensure that the transfer function of this LTI system is
[latex]H(s)=\frac{1}{s^3+3s^2+2s+1}[/latex]?
questions.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} X(t) &=A x(t)+B u(t) \\ y(t) &=C x(t) \\ B &=\left[\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}\right] \\ \frac{\gamma(s)}{U(s)} &=\\ \frac{\gamma(s)}{X_{1}(s)} \times \frac{X_{1}(s)}{U(s)}=& 1 \times \frac{1}{s^{3}+3 s^{2}+2 s+1} \\ x_{1}(s)\left(s^{3}+3 s^{2}+2 s+1\right]&=U(s) \\ x_{2} &=\dot{x}_{1}(t) \\ x_{2}(s) &=s x_{1}(s) \\ x_{3} &=\dot{x}_{2}(t) \\ \Rightarrow \quad x_{3}(s) &=s x_{2}(s)=s^{2} X_{1}(s) \\ \text { So, } \quad s x_{3}(s) &=-x_{1}(s)-2 x_{2}(s)-3 x_{3}(s)+u(s) \\ \dot{x}_{3}(t) &=-x_{1}(t)-2 r_{2}(t)-3 x_{3}(t)+u(t) \\ y(t) &=x_{1}(t) \\ \dot{x}(t) &=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -3\end{array}\right] x(t)+\left[\begin{array}{l}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{array}\right] u(t) \\ y(t) &=[1 \quad 0 \quad 0] x(t) \end{aligned}[/latex]

Transfer function
[latex]\begin{aligned} T(s) &=\frac{Y(s)}{U(s)}=\mathrm{C}(s I-A]^{-1} \mathrm{B} \\ A &=\left[\begin{array}{cc} -4 & -1.5 \\ 4 & 0 \end{array}\right] \\ B &=\left[\begin{array}{c} 2 \\ 0 \end{array}\right] \\ C&=[1.5\quad0.625]\\ {[s I-A]} & =\left[\begin{array}{cc}s+4 & 1.5 \\-4 & s\end{array}\right] \\ {[s I-A]^{-1}} & =\frac{1}{\left(s^{2}+4 s+6\right)}\left[\begin{array}{cc}s & -1.5 \\4 & s+4 \end{array}\right] \\ {[s I-A]^{-1} B} & =\frac{1}{s^{2}+4 s+6}\left[\begin{array}{c}2 s \\8 \end{array}\right] & \\ C[s I-A]^{-1} B & =\frac{1}{s^{2}+4 s+6}[1.5 \quad 0.625]\left[\begin{array}{c}2 s \\ 8\end{array}\right] \\ T(s) & =\frac{3 s+5}{s^{2}+4 s+6} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text:
A second - order LTI system is described by the following state equations,
[latex]\frac{d}{dt}x_{1}(t)- x_{2}(t)=0[/latex]
[latex]\frac{d}{dt}x_{2}(t)+2x_{1}(t)+3x_{2}(t)=r(t)[/latex]
Where [latex] x_{1}(t)[/latex] and [latex]x_{2}(t)[/latex] are the two state variables and r(t) denotes the input. The output [latex] c(t) =x_{1}(t)[/latex]. The system is.
questions.solution:
Given state variable equations are as follows:
[latex] \begin{aligned} &\frac{d}{d t} x_{1}(t)-x_{2}(t)=0 &\ldots(i)\\ &\frac{d}{d t} x_{2}(t)+2 x_{2}(t)+3 x_{2}(t)=r(t) &\ldots(ii) \end{aligned}[/latex]
Also given that, input [latex]=r(t)[/latex] and output [latex]=x_{1}(t) [/latex]
By applying Laplace transform to equation (i), we
get,
[latex] s X_{1}(s)=X_{2}(s) \qquad \ldots(iii)[/latex]
By applying Laplace transform to equation (ii).
we get,
[latex] \begin{aligned} s X_{2}(s)+2 X_{1}(s)+3 X_{2}(s)&=R(s) \\ x_{2}(s)&=\frac{R(s)-2 X_{1}(s)}{s+3} &\ldots(iv) \end{aligned}[/latex]
By substituting equation (iv) in equation (iii), we get,
[latex] \begin{aligned} s X_{\mathrm{i}}(s)&=\frac{R(s)-2 X_{1}(s)}{s+3}\\ \left(s^{2}+3 s+2\right) X_{1}(s)&=R(s) \end{aligned}[/latex]
So, the transfer function of the given system is,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{X_{1}(s)}{R(s)} &=\frac{1}{s^{2}+3 s+2} \\ v r^{2} &=2 \\ 2 \zeta_{n} &=3 \\ \xi &=\frac{3}{2 \omega_{n}}=\frac{3}{2 \sqrt{2}}=1.06 \end{aligned}[/latex]
As [latex]\xi \gt 1,[/latex] the given system is overdamped.

questions.text:
Consider the state space realization
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} x_{1}(t)\\ x_{2}(t) \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0\\ 0&-9 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x_{1}(t)\\ x_{2}(t) \end{bmatrix}+ \begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 45 \end{bmatrix}u(t)[/latex] , with the initial condition [latex]\begin{bmatrix} x_{1}(0)\\ x_{2}(0) \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
where u(t) denotes the unit step function. The value of [latex]\lim_{t\rightarrow \infty }|\sqrt{x_{1}^{2}(t)+x_{2}^{2}(t)}|[/latex] is _______.
questions.solution:
[latex]\left[\begin{array}{l} \dot{x}_{1}(t) \\ \dot{x}_{2}(t) \end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{cc} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l} x_{1}(t) \\ x_{2}(t) \end{array}\right]+\left[\begin{array}{c} 0 \\ 45 \end{array}\right] u(t)[/latex]
By applying Laplace transform on both sides. get
[latex] \begin{aligned} s x_{1}(s)-x_{1}(0)&=0\\ X_{1}(s)&=\frac{x_{1}(0)}{s}=0 \quad \because x_{1}(0)=0 \\ \text{So,} x_{1}(t)&=0 \\ \text{and }\quad s X_{\lambda}(s)-x_{2}(0)&=-9 X_{1}(s)+\frac{45}{s} \\ X_{2}(s) &=\frac{45}{s(s+9)} \quad \because x_{2}(0)=0 \\ \text { Required value } &=\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty}|\sqrt{x_{1}^{2}(t)+x_{2}^{2}(t)}| \\ &=\left|\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} x_{2}(t)\right| \quad \because x_{1}(t)=0 \\ \lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} x_{2}(t) &=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} s X_{2}(s)=\frac{45}{9}=5 \end{aligned}[/latex]
So,
Required value [latex]= |5| =5[/latex]

[latex]\begin{bmatrix} \frac{d\omega }{dt}\\ \frac{di_{a}}{dt} \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 & 1\\ -1&-10 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} \omega \\ i_{a} \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 10 \end{bmatrix}u[/latex]
where [latex]\omega[/latex] is the speed of the motor, [latex]i_{a}[/latex] is the armature current and u is the armature voltage. The transfer function [latex]\frac{\omega (s)}{U(s)}[/latex] of the motor is
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \left[\begin{array}{c}\frac{d \omega}{d t} \\\frac{d i_{a}}{d t}\end{array}\right]&=\left[\begin{array}{cc} -1 & 1 \\ -1 & -10 \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l} \omega \\ i_{a} \end{array}\right]+\left[\begin{array}{c} 0 \\ 10 \end{array}\right] u\\ \Rightarrow \frac{d \omega}{d t}&=-\omega+i_{\mathrm{a}} &\ldots(i)\\ \Rightarrow \frac{d i_{\mathrm{a}}}{d t}&=-\omega-10 i_{\mathrm{a}}+10 u &\ldots(ii) \end{aligned}[/latex]
Taking Laplace transform (i) \& (ii)
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow s \omega(s)=-\omega(s)+I_{a}(s) \\ \Rightarrow(s+1) \omega(s)=I_{a}(s) \quad\ldots(iii)\\ \Rightarrow s I_{e}(s)=-\omega(s)-10 I_{a}(s)+10 U(s) \\ \Rightarrow \omega(s)=(-10-s) I_{a}(s)+10 U(s) \\ =(-10-s)(s+1) \omega(s)+10 U(s) \\ =-\left[s^{2}+11 s+10\right] \omega(s)+10 U(s) \\ \Rightarrow\left[s^{2}+11 s+11\right] \omega(s)=10 U(s) \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\omega(s)}{U(s)}=\frac{10}{\left(s^{2}+11 s+11\right)} \end{array}[/latex]

questions.text:
The state variable equations of a system are :
1. [latex]\dot{x_{1}}=-3x_{1}-x_{2}+u[/latex]
2. [latex]\dot{x_{2}}=2x_{1}[/latex]
[latex]y=x_{1}+u[/latex]
The system is
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \left[\begin{array}{c}\dot{x}_{1} \\\dot{x}_{2}\end{array}\right]&=\left[\begin{array}{cc}-3 & -1 \\2 & 0\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x_{1} \\x_{2}\end{array}\right]+\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\0\end{array}\right] u \\ y&=\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 0\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x_{1} \\x_{2}\end{array}\right]+\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\0\end{array}\right] u \\ Q_{C}&=\left[\begin{array}{ll}B & A B\end{array}\right]\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} A B&=\left[\begin{array}{c}-3 \\ 2\end{array}\right] \\ \therefore \quad a_{c}&=\left[\begin{array}{cc}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 2\end{array}\right] \neq 0 \\ \therefore \text{Controllable } \\ Q_{0}&=\left[C^{\top} \quad A^{\top} C^{\prime}\right] \\ C^{T}&=\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\ 0\end{array}\right], \quad A^{T}&=\left[\begin{array}{ll}-3 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{array}\right] \\ A^{\top} C^{T}&=\left[\begin{array}{l}-3 \\ -1\end{array}\right] \\ \therefore \quad Q_{0}&=\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & -3 \\ 0 & -1\end{array}\right] \neq 0 \\ \therefore \text{ Observable} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: The transfer function Y(s)U(s) of a system described by the state equations x(t) = -2x(t) + 2u(t) and y(t) = 0.5x(t) is

[latex]\begin{aligned} \dot{x}(t)=-2 x(t)+2 u(t) &\ldots(i)\\ y(t)=0.5 x(t)&\ldots(ii) \end{aligned}[/latex]
From (i), Taking Laplace transform of (i)
[latex] \begin{aligned} s X(s)&=-2 X(s)+2 U(s)\\ X(s)[s+2]&=2 U(s)\\ \Rightarrow \quad X(s)&=\frac{2 U(s)}{(s+2)} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Taking Laplace transform of (ii)
[latex] \begin{aligned} Y(s)&=0.5 X(s) \\ Y(s)&=\frac{0.5 \times 2 U(s)}{s+2} \\ \therefore \quad \frac{Y(s)}{U(s)}&=\frac{1}{(s+2)} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider a real, narrowband signal [latex]x(t) = A(t)\cos[2\pi f_ct + \theta(t)][/latex] where the maximum frequency components of [latex]A(t)[/latex] and [latex]\theta(t)[/latex] are [latex]f_M[/latex] and [latex]f_c (= 1000 f_M)[/latex], respectively.

Which of the following statements is/are correct for [latex]-\infty < t < \infty[/latex]?
options: [latex]x(t)[/latex] represents a PSK modulated signal for suitable choices of [latex]A(t)[/latex] and [latex]\theta(t)[/latex]
[latex]x(t)[/latex] represents an amplitude modulated signal for suitable choices of [latex]A(t)[/latex] and [latex]\theta(t)[/latex].
[latex]x(t)[/latex] represents a band-limited Gaussian noise process.
[latex]x(t)[/latex] never represents a narrowband FM signal.
questions.solution:
Given narrow band signal, [latex] x(t)=A(t)\cos[2\pi f_c t+\theta(t)] [/latex]
  • For suitable choices of [latex] A(t) [/latex] and [latex] \theta(t) [/latex], [latex] x(t) [/latex] represents an AM signal.

    Example: Let
    [latex] A(t)=1+m(t) [/latex]
    [latex] \theta(t)=0 [/latex]
    Then,
    [latex] x(t)=[1+m(t)]\cos 2\pi f_c t [/latex]
    Thus, it represents an AM signal.

  • For suitable choices of [latex] A(t) [/latex] and [latex] \theta(t) [/latex], [latex] x(t) [/latex] represents a PSK signal.

    Example: Let [latex] A(t) [/latex] be constant and

    [latex] \theta(t)=45^\circ,\ 135^\circ,\ 225^\circ,\ 315^\circ [/latex]
    Hence, [latex] x(t) [/latex] represents a PSK signal.

  • [latex] x(t) [/latex] represents a bandlimited Gaussian noise process.

    Writing,
    [latex] x(t)=x_I(t)\cos 2\pi f_c t - x_Q(t)\sin 2\pi f_c t [/latex]
    where,

    [latex] x_I(t)=A(t)\cos\theta(t) [/latex]
    [latex] x_Q(t)=A(t)\sin\theta(t) [/latex]
    If [latex] x_I(t) [/latex] and [latex] x_Q(t) [/latex] are Gaussian processes, then [latex] x(t) [/latex] also represents a Gaussian process.

    Hence, options (A), (B), and (C) are correct.
Now consider option (D).

Example:

[latex] x(t)=A(t)\cos[2\pi f_c t+\theta(t)] [/latex]
Here, the term [latex] \theta(t) [/latex] represents angle modulation. Therefore, [latex] x(t) [/latex] can also represent an NBFM signal.

Hence, option (D) is incorrect.

questions.text:
Consider a message signal [latex]\mathrm{m}(\mathrm{t})[/latex] which is bandlimited to [latex][-\mathrm{W}, \mathrm{W}][/latex], where W is in Hz . Consider the following two modulation schemes for the message signal:

Double sideband-suppressed carrier (DSB-SC):
[latex]f_{D S B}(t)=A_{c} m(t) \cos \left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right)[/latex]

Amplitude modulation (AM):
[latex]f_{A M}(t)=A_{c}(1+\mu m(t)) \cos \left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right)[/latex]

Here, [latex]A_{c}[/latex] and [latex]f_{c}[/latex] are the amplitude and frequency (in Hz ) of the carrier, respectively. In the case of AM, [latex]\mu[/latex] denotes the modulation index.

Consider the following statements:
(i) An envelope detector can be used for demodulation in the DSB-SC scheme if [latex]\mathrm{m}(\mathrm{t})>0[/latex] for all t .
(ii) An envelope detector can be used for demodulation in the AM scheme only if [latex]\mathrm{m}(\mathrm{t})>0[/latex] for all t .

Which of the following options is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Even if [latex] m(t) > 0 [/latex] for all [latex] t [/latex], the carrier is suppressed, and therefore envelope detection fails.
So, Statement (i) is FALSE.

Statement (ii): In standard AM, the transmitted signal is:
[latex] f_{AM}(t) = A_c (1 + \mu m(t)) \cos(2\pi f_c t) [/latex]
To ensure proper envelope detection, the envelope [latex] A_c(1 + \mu m(t)) [/latex] must not cross zero, i.e., it must be always positive.
So the condition is: [latex] 1 + \mu m(t) > 0 [/latex] for all [latex] t [/latex]. This means not just [latex] m(t) > 0 [/latex], but [latex] m(t) > -1/\mu [/latex]. So even if [latex] m(t) [/latex] is not strictly positive, envelope detection may still work depending on [latex] \mu [/latex].
Therefore, Statement (ii) is FALSE.

questions.text:
Consider a frequency-modulated (FM) signal

[latex] f(t) = A_c \cos\left(2\pi f_c t + 3\sin(2\pi f_1 t) + 4\sin(6\pi f_1 t)\right) [/latex],

where [latex] A_c [/latex] and [latex] f_c [/latex] are, respectively, the amplitude and frequency (in Hz) of the carrier waveform. The frequency [latex] f_1 [/latex] is in Hz, and assume that [latex] f_c > 100f_1 [/latex].

The peak frequency deviation of the FM signal in Hz is _______.
questions.solution:
The general form of an FM signal is: [latex] f(t) = A_c \cos\left(2\pi f_c t + \phi(t)\right) [/latex],
where [latex] \phi(t) [/latex] is the instantaneous phase deviation.

Here, [latex] \phi(t) = 3\sin(2\pi f_1 t) + 4\sin(6\pi f_1 t) [/latex]

To find instantaneous frequency deviation, we take the derivative of [latex] \phi(t) [/latex]:

[latex] \frac{d\phi(t)}{dt} = 3 \cdot 2\pi f_1 \cos(2\pi f_1 t) + 4 \cdot 6\pi f_1 \cos(6\pi f_1 t) [/latex]
[latex] = 6\pi f_1 \cos(2\pi f_1 t) + 24\pi f_1 \cos(6\pi f_1 t) [/latex]

So, instantaneous frequency deviation:
[latex] \Delta f(t) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \frac{d\phi(t)}{dt} = 3f_1 \cos(2\pi f_1 t) + 12f_1 \cos(6\pi f_1 t) [/latex]

Peak frequency deviation is the maximum absolute value of [latex] \Delta f(t) [/latex]:
[latex] \Delta f_{\text{peak}} = \max|\Delta f(t)| = 3f_1 + 12f_1 = 15f_1 [/latex]

questions.text:
An amplitude modulator has output (in Volts)

[latex] s(t)=A \cos (400 \pi t)+B \cos (360 \pi t)+B \cos (440 \pi t) [/latex]

The carrier power normalized to [latex]1 \Omega[/latex] resistance is 50 Watts. The ratio of the total sideband power to the total power is [latex]1 / 9[/latex]. The value of [latex]B[/latex] (in Volts. rounded off to two decimal places) is ______
questions.solution: [latex] \begin{aligned} P_{C} & =\frac{A^{2}}{2}=50 \\ A & =10 \\ \frac{P_{S B}}{P_{t}} & =\frac{\mu^{2}}{2+\mu^{2}}=\frac{1}{9} \\ \mu & =\frac{1}{2} \\ B & =\frac{A_{c} \mu}{2}=\frac{10}{2} \times \frac{1}{2}=2.5 \end{aligned} [/latex]

questions.text: Let a frequency modulated (FM) signal [latex]x(t)=A \cos \left(\omega_{c} t+k_{f} \int_{-\infty}^{t} m(\lambda) d \lambda\right)[/latex], where [latex]m(t)[/latex] is a message signal of bandwidth [latex]W[/latex]. It is passed through a non-linear system with output [latex]y(t)=2 x(t)+5(x(t))^{2}[/latex]. Let [latex]B_{T}[/latex] denote the FM bandwidth. The minimum value of [latex]\omega_{c}[/latex] required to recover [latex]x(t)[/latex] from [latex]y(t)[/latex] is
questions.solution:
[latex] x(t)=A \cos \left[\omega_{c} t+K_{f} \int_{-\infty}^{t} m(\lambda) d \lambda\right] [/latex]
B.W. [latex][x(t)] \rightarrow B T=2[\Delta f+\omega][/latex]

[latex] \left.x^{2}(t) \rightarrow \begin{array}{c} \Delta f^{\prime}=2 \Delta f \\ \omega_{c}^{\prime}=2 \omega_{c} \end{array}\right\} [/latex]

[latex]\mathrm{BW}\left[x^{2}(t)\right]=2\left[\Delta f^{\prime}+\omega\right][/latex] [latex]=2[2 \Delta f+\omega]=B T+2 \Delta f[/latex]
[latex]y(t)=2x(t)+5x^2(t) [/latex]

To recover [latex]x(t) \rightarrow \quad 2 \omega_{C}-\frac{B_{T}}{2}-\Delta f \gt \omega_{C}+\frac{B_{T}}{2}[/latex]
[latex]\omega_{c} \gt \Delta f+B T[/latex]
[latex]\omega_{c} \gt \Delta f+2 \Delta f+2 \omega[/latex]
[latex]\omega_{c} \gt 3 \Delta f+2 \omega[/latex]
[latex]\omega_{c} \gt \frac{3}{2}\{2[\Delta f+\omega]\}-\omega[/latex]
[latex]\omega_{c} \gt \frac{3}{2} B_{T}-\omega[/latex]
Compared to FM BW, message BW is very small. So, that it can be ignored.
[latex] \begin{aligned} \omega_{C} & \gt \frac{3}{2} B_{T} \\ \left[\omega_{C}\right]_{min } & =\frac{3}{2} B_{T} \end{aligned} [/latex]

questions.text: The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of an ADC with a full-scale sinusoidal input is given to be [latex]61.96 \mathrm{~dB}[/latex]. The resolution of the ADC is _____ bits. (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.solution:
We know that for sinusoidal input, the signal to noise ratio (SNR) is given as,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \mathrm{SNR} & =1.76+6.02 \mathrm{n} \mathrm{dB} \\ 61.96 \mathrm{~dB} & =1.76+6.02 \mathrm{n} \mathrm{dB} \\ 6.02 \mathrm{n} & =61.96-1.76 \\ n & =10 \text { bits } \end{aligned} [/latex]

questions.text: Consider a superheterodyne receiver tuned to [latex]600 \text{ kHz}[/latex]. If the local oscillator feeds a [latex]1000 \text{ kHz}[/latex]  signal to the mixer, the image frequency (in integer) is ____________________ [latex]\text{kHz}[/latex] .
questions.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} f_{s} &=600 \mathrm{kHz} \\ f_{l} &=1000 \mathrm{kHz} \\ f_{s i} &=? \\ \text { Default } f_{l}>f_{s} & \\ \mathrm{IF} &=f_{l}-f_{s}=400 \mathrm{kHz} \\ f_{\mathrm{si}} &=f_{s}+2 \mathrm{IF}=600 \mathrm{~K}+800 \mathrm{~K}=1400 \mathrm{kHz} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: A sinusoidal message signal having root mean square value of [latex]4\:V[/latex]  and frequency of [latex]\text{1 kHz}[/latex]  is fed to a phase modulator with phase deviation constant 2 rad/ volt. If the carrier signal is [latex]c\left ( t \right )=2\cos\left ( 2\pi 10^{6} t\right )[/latex], the maximum instantaneous frequency of the phase modulated signal (rounded off to one decimal place) is ______ [latex]\text{Hz}[/latex] .
questions.solution:
Given sinusoidal message signal [latex]\rightarrow V_{\mathrm{rms}}=4 \mathrm{~V}[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} f_{m} &=1 \mathrm{kHz} \\ V_{\text {peak }} &=\sqrt{2} \times V_{\mathrm{rms}}=\sqrt{2} \times 4 \mathrm{~V} \\ m(t) &=4 \sqrt{2} \sin 2 \pi \times 10^{3} t\\ K_{p}&=2 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{volt}\\ c(t) &=2 \cos 2 \pi \times 10^{6} \mathrm{t} \\ \left(f_{i}\right)_{\max } &=f_{c}+\frac{K_{p}}{2 \pi}\left[\frac{d}{d t} m(t)\right]_{\max } \\ \frac{d}{d t} m(t) &=4 \sqrt{2} \times\left(2 \pi \times 10^{3}\right) \cos 2 \pi \times 10^{3} t \\ \left[\frac{d}{d t} m(t)\right]_{\max } &=4 \sqrt{2} \times 2 \pi \times 10^{3} \\ \left(f_{i}\right)_{\max } &=10^{6}+\frac{2}{2 \pi}\left(4 \sqrt{2} \times 2 \pi \times 10^{3}\right)=1011313.7 \mathrm{~Hz} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: A [latex]4\:kHz[/latex] sinusoidal message signal having amplitude [latex]4\:V[/latex] is fed to a delta modulator (DM) operating at a sampling rate of [latex]32\:\text{kHz}[/latex] . The minimum step size required to avoid slope overload noise in the DM (rounded off to two decimal places) is _____
questions.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} f_{m}&=4 \mathrm{kHz} \\ A_{m}&=4 \mathrm{~V} \\ f_{s}&=32 \mathrm{kHz}\\ \text { To avoid } \text{SOE} \rightarrow &\frac{\Delta}{T_{s}} \geq 2 \pi f_{m} A_{m} \\ \Delta \times 32 k &\geq 2 \pi \times 4 k \times 4 \mathrm{~V} \\ \Delta &\geq \pi\\ (\Delta)_{\min }&=\pi volts\\ (\Delta)_{\min }&=3.14 volts \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: Consider a carrier signal which is amplitude modulated by a single-tone sinusoidal message signal with a modulation index of [latex]50\%[/latex]. If the carrier and one of the sidebands are suppressed in the modulated signal, the percentage of power saved (rounded off to one decimal place) is ______________
questions.solution:
If carrier and one of the sidebands are suppressed, then % of power saved
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=\frac{\text { Power saved }}{\text { Total power }}=\frac{P_{c}+\frac{P_{c} \mu^{2}}{4}}{P_{c}\left[1+\frac{\mu^{2}}{2}\right]}=\frac{4+\mu^{2}}{4+2 \mu^{2}} \\ &=\frac{4+(0.5)^{2}}{4+2 \times(0.5)^{2}}=0.944=94.4 \% \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text:
[latex]S_{PM}(t)\; and \; S_{FM}(t)[/latex] as defined below, are the phase modulated and the frequency modulated waveforms, respectively, corresponding to the message signal m(t) shown in the figure.

[latex]S_{PM}(t)= \cos (1000 \pi t+K_p m(t))[/latex]
and [latex]S_{FM}(t)= \cos (1000 \pi t+K_f \int_{-\infty }^{t} m(\tau )d\tau )[/latex]

where [latex]K_p[/latex] is the phase deviation constant in radians/volt and [latex]K_f[/latex] is the frequency deviation constant in radians/second/volt. If the highest instantaneous frequencies of [latex]S_{PM}(t)\; and \; S_{FM}(t)[/latex] are same, then the value of the ratio [latex]\frac{K_p}{K_f}[/latex] is ______ seconds.
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned}S(t)_{pm}&=A_c \cos [2\pi f_{c}t+k_pm(t)]\\ S(t)_{Fm}&=A_c \cos [2\pi f_{c}t+k_{f}\int_{0}^{\infty }m(t)dt]\end{aligned}[/latex]
Instantaneous frequency are equal
[latex]\begin{aligned}f_{i}&=\frac{1}{2\pi }\frac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t}\theta (t)\\f_{iPM}&=f_{c}+\frac{K_p}{2\pi }\frac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t} m(t)\\ f_{iFM}&=f_{c}+\frac{K_f}{2\pi }m(t)\\ \text{Given that, } (f_{iPM})_{max}&=(f_{iFM})_{max} \\ f_{c}+\frac{k_P}{2\pi}[\frac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t}m(t)]_{max}&=f_{c}+\frac{K_{f}}{2\pi }[m(t)]_{max}\\ \left.\begin{matrix} \frac{k_P}{2\pi}\frac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t}m(t) \end{matrix}\right|_{max} &= \left. \begin{matrix} \frac{K_{f}}{2\pi }[m(t)] \end{matrix}\right|_{max}\\ \left.\begin{matrix} \frac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t}m(t) \end{matrix}\right|_{max} &=5, \left.\begin{matrix} m(t) \end{matrix}\right|_{max}=10 \\ 5k_{p}&=10k_{f} \\ \frac{k_{p}}{k_{f}}&=2\end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: For the modulated signal [latex]x(t)= m(t) \cos(2 \pi f_c t)[/latex], the message signal [latex]m(t) = 4 \cos (1000 \pi t)[/latex] and the carrier frequency [latex]f_c[/latex] is 1 MHz. The signal [latex]x(t)[/latex] is passed through a demodulator, as shown in the figure below. The output [latex]y(t)[/latex] of the demodulator is
questions.solution:
Output of multiplier
[latex]=x(t)\cos 2\pi (f_{c}+40)t=m(t)\cos 2\pi f_{c}t\cdot \cos2\pi (f_{c}+40)t[/latex]
[latex] =\frac{m(t)}{2}[\cos 2\pi (2f_{c}+40)t+\cos 2\pi (40)t][/latex]
Given, [latex]m(t)=4\cos 1000\pi t[/latex]
So, output of multiplier
[latex]=2\cos 2\pi (500)t[\cos 2\pi (2f_{c}+40)t+\cos 2\pi (40)t][/latex]
[latex]=\cos 2\pi (2f_{c}+540)t+\cos 2\pi (2f_{c}-460)t+\cos 2\pi (540)t+\cos 2\pi (460)t[/latex]
Output of Low pass filter
[latex]=\cos [2\pi (460)]t[/latex]
[latex] =\cos 920\pi t[/latex]

questions.text: The baseband signal m(t) shown in the figure is phase-modulated to generate the PM signal [latex]\varphi (t)=2cos(2 \pi f_c t+km(t))[/latex]. The time t on the x-axis in the figure is in milliseconds. If the carrier frequency is [latex]f_c[/latex]=50kHz and [latex]k=10 \pi[/latex], then the ratio of the minimum instantaneous frequency (in kHz) to the maximum instantaneous frequency (in kHz) is __________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} f_i&=\frac{1}{2 \pi}\frac{d\theta (t)}{dt}= \\ &=f_c+\frac{k}{2 \pi}\frac{dm (t)}{dt} \\ &=f_c+5\frac{dm (t)}{dt} \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned} f_{i(min)}&=50kHz-(5 \times 1000Hz)=45kHz\\ f_{i(max)}&=50kHz+(5 \times 2000Hz)=60kHz\\ \frac{f_{i(min)}}{f_{i(max)}}&=\frac{45}{60}=0.75 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: Let [latex] c(t)=A_{c} cos(2\pi f_{c}t) \; and  \; m(t)=cos(2\pi f_{m}t) [/latex]. It is given that [latex] f_{c}>>5f_{m} [/latex]. The signal [latex] c(t) +m(t) [/latex]  is applied to the input of a non-linear device, whose output [latex] v_{o}(t) [/latex] is related to the input [latex] v_{i}(t)+bv_{i}(t) [/latex],where a and b  are positive constants. The output of the non-linear device is passed through an ideal band-pass filter with center frequency [latex] f_{c} [/latex] and bandwidth [latex] 3f_{m}[/latex] ,to produce an amplitude modulated (AM) wave. If it is desired to have the sideband power of the AM wave to be half of the carrier power, then [latex]a/b[/latex] is
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} v_{f t}^{(t)} &=A_{c} \cos \left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right)+\cos \left(2 \pi t_{m} t\right) \\ v_{d}(t) &=a v_{i}(t)+b v_{i}^{2}(t) \\ =&\left[a A_{c} \cos \left(2 \pi t_{c} t\right)+a \cos \left(2 \pi f_{m} t\right)\right] \\ \quad &+b\left[\begin{array}{c}A_{c}^{2} \cos ^{2}\left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right)+\cos ^{2}\left(2 \pi f_{m} t\right) \\ +2 A_{c} \cos \left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right) \cos \left(2 \pi t_{m} t\right)\end{array}\right] \end{aligned} [/latex]
After passing through the given BPF,
[latex] y(t)=a A_{c} \cos 2 \pi f_{c} t+2 b A_{c} \cos \left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right) \cos \left(2 \pi f_{m} t\right) [/latex]
[latex] =a A_{c}\left[1+\frac{2 b}{a} \cos \left(2 \pi f_{m} t\right)\right] \cos \left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right) [/latex]
Modulation index,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \mu &=\begin{array}{l}2 b \\ a\end{array} \\ P_{S B} &=\frac{\mu^{2}}{2} P_{C}=\frac{1}{2} P_{C} \\ \mu^{2} &=1 \Rightarrow \mu=1 \\ \frac{2 b}{a} &=1 \\ \frac{a}{b} &=2 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: Consider the following amplitude modulated signal: [latex]s(t)=cos(2000\pi t)+4cos(2400\pi t)+cos(2800\pi t).[/latex] The ratio (accurate to three decimal places) of the power of the message signal to the power of the carrier signal is __________.
questions.solution:
The power of the carrier signal is,
[latex] P_{c}=\frac{(4)^{2}}{2}=8 \mathrm{W}[/latex]
The power of message signal can be taken as the power carried by the sidebands.
So, the power of the message signal is,
[latex] P_{m}=2\left[\frac{(1)^{2}}{2}\right]=1 \mathrm{W}[/latex]
Required ratio,
[latex] \frac{P_{m}}{P_{c}}=\frac{1}{8}=0.125[/latex]

questions.text: A modulating signal given By [latex] x(t) =5sin(4 \pi 10^{3}t-10\pi cos2\pi 10^{3}t[/latex])V is fed to a phase modulator with phase deviation constant [latex]k_{p}[/latex]=0.5rad/V. If the carrier frequency is 20 kHz, the instantaneous frequency (in kHz) at t = 0.5 ms is __________
questions.solution:
Given that, the modulating signal is.
[latex] x(t)=5 \sin (4000 \pi t-10 \pi \cos 2000 \pi t) \mathrm{V}[/latex]
The standard phase modulated signal can be given as,
[latex] s(t)=A_{c} \cos \left(\omega_{c} t+k_{p} x(t)\right)[/latex]
Instantaneous angle of the modulated signal is.
[latex] \theta(t)=\omega_{c} t+k_{p} x(t)[/latex]
Instantaneous frequency is,
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \omega_{1}(t)=\frac{d \theta(t)}{d t}\\ =\omega_{c}+k_{p} \frac{d x(t)}{d t} \\ f_{i}(t)=f_{c}+\frac{25}{2 \pi}[\cos (4000 \pi t-10 \pi \cos 2000 \pi t) \\ \quad \left.\left(4000 \pi+20000 \pi^{2} \sin 2000 \pi t\right)\right] \\ A t=0.5 \mathrm{ms} \\ \begin{aligned} f_{1}(t)=& f_{c}+\frac{25}{2 \pi}[\cos (2 \pi-10 \pi \cos (\pi))] \\ &\quad\left(4000 \pi+20000 \pi^{2} \sin (\pi)\right) & \\ &=f_{c}+\frac{25}{2 \pi}[\cos (12 \pi)](4000 \pi) \\ &=f_{c}+50 \mathrm{kHz} \\ =& 70 \mathrm{kHz} \; \; ( \because \text { Given that, } f_{c}=20 \mathrm{kHz}) \end{aligned} \end{array}[/latex]

questions.text: The un-modulated carrier power in an AM transmitter is 5kW. This carrier is modulated by a sinusoidal modulating signal. The maximum percentage of modulation is 50%. If it is reduced to 40%, then the maximum un-modulated carrier power (in kW) that can be used without overloading the transmitter is ___________
questions.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text { Given that, } P_{C}&=5 \mathrm{kW} \text { for } \mu_{(\mathrm{max})}=0.5\\ \text { So, } \quad P_{t(\max )}&=P_{c}\left[1+\frac{(0.5)^{2}}{2}\right]\\ &=5\left[1+\frac{0.25}{2}\right] \mathrm{kW}=5.625 \mathrm{kW} \\ \text { For } \mu & =0.4,\\ &\begin{aligned} P_{ \text {Qrex } )}\left(1+\frac{\mu^{2}}{2}\right)=&P_{t(\max )} \\ P_{C(\text{rax})}=& \frac{5.625}{1+\frac{(0.4)^{2}}{2}} \mathrm{kW} \\ & =5.208 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: For a superheterodyne receiver, the intermediate frequency is 15 MHz and the local oscillator frequency is 3.5 GHz. If the frequency of the received signal is greater than the local oscillator frequency, then the image frequency (in MHz) is __________
questions.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} I F &=15 \mathrm{MHz} \\ f_{l} &=3.5 \mathrm{GHz} \\ f_{\mathrm{si}} &=f_{l}-\mathrm{IF} \\ &=3500-15 \mathrm{MHz}=3485 \mathrm{MHz} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: The amplitude of a sinusoidal carrier is modulated by a single sinusoid to obtain the amplitude modulated signal [latex]s(t)=5 cos 1600\pi t+20 cos 1800\pi t +5cos 2000 \pi t[/latex]. The value of the modulation index is __________
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} s(t)=& 5 \cos 1600 \pi t+20 \cos 1800 \pi t+5 \cos 2000 \pi t \\ s(t)=& 20 \cos 1800 \pi t+5 \cos 1600 \pi t+5 \cos 200 \pi t \\ s(t)=& A_{c} \cos 2 \pi f_{c} t+\frac{A_{c} \mu}{2} \cos 2 \pi\left(f_{c}-t_{m}\right) t \\ &+\frac{A_{c} \mu}{2} \cos 2 \pi\left(f_{c}+f_{m}\right) t \end{aligned}[/latex]
comparing, we get
[latex] \begin{aligned} A_{c}&=20 \mathrm{v} ; \frac{A_{c} \mu}{2}=5 \mathrm{V}\\ \mu&=\frac{10}{20}=0.5 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: A superheterodyne receiver operates in the frequency range of 58 MHz - 68 MHz. The intermediate frequency [latex]f_{IF}[/latex] and local oscillator frequency [latex]f_{LO}[/latex] are chosen such that [latex]f_{IF}[/latex] [latex]\leq f_{LO}[/latex] . It is required that the image frequencies fall outside t he 58 MHz - 68 MHz band. The minimum required [latex]f_{IF}[/latex] (in MHz) is ________
questions.solution:
[latex]f_{s}=58 \mathrm{MHz}-68 \mathrm{MHz} [/latex]
[latex] f_{s l}[/latex] should fall outside the range [latex]58 \mathrm{MHz}-68 \mathrm{MHz}[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text { Hence } \quad f_{\text {smin }} &=58 \mathrm{MHz} \\ f_{\mathrm{si}} &=f_{s}+2 I F \gt 68 \mathrm{MHz} \\ 58 \mathrm{MHz}+2 I F & \gt 68 \mathrm{MHz} \\ I F & \gt 5 \mathrm{MHz} \\ \Rightarrow (I F)_{\min }&=5 \mathrm{MHz} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text:
The block diagram of a frequency synthesizer consisting of a Phase Locked Loop (PLL) and a divide-by-N counter (comprising [latex]\div[/latex] 2 ,[latex]\div[/latex] 4, [latex]\div[/latex] 8, [latex]\div[/latex] 16 outputs) is sketched below. The synthesizer is excited with a 5 kHz signal (Input 1). The free-running frequency of the PLL is set to 20 kHz. Assume that the commutator switch makes contacts repeatedly in the order 1-2-3-4.

The corresponding frequencies synthesized are:
The complex envelope of the bandpass signal [latex]x(t)=-\sqrt{2}(\frac{sin(\pi t/ 5)}{\pi t/ 5})sin(\pi -\frac{\pi}{4})[/latex] , centered about [latex]f=\frac{1}{2}[/latex] Hz, is
questions.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} x(t) &=-\sqrt{2}\left[\frac{\sin \left(\frac{\pi t}{5}\right)}{\left(\frac{\pi t}{5}\right)}\right] \sin \left(\pi t-\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \\ x(t) &=\text{Re}\left[\tilde{x}(t) e^{i 2 \pi t_{c} t}\right] \\ \tilde{x}(t) &=\text { Complex envelope } \\ &=\sqrt{2}\left[\frac{\sin \left(\frac{\pi t}{5}\right)}{\left(\frac{\pi t}{5}\right)}\right] e^{i \pi / 4} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: A message signal [latex]m(t)=A_{m} sin(2\pi f_{m}f)[/latex] is used to modulate the phase of a carrier [latex]A_{c}cos(2\pi f_{c}t)[/latex] to get the modulated signal [latex]y(t)=A_{c} cos(2\pi f_{c}t+m(t))[/latex].  The bandwidth of y(t).
options: does not depend on [latex]A_{m} or f_{m}[/latex]
questions.solution:
The bandwidth of a PM signal is given by
[latex] B=2\left(\Delta f+f_{m}\right)[/latex]
Now, for single tone PM signal
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Delta f&=A_{m} K_{\rho} f_{m} \\ \therefore \quad B&=2\left(K_{p} A_{m}+1\right) f_{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: In the system shown in Figure (a), m(t) is a low-pass signal with bandwidth W Hz. The frequency response of the band-pass filter H(f) is shown in Figure (b). If it is desired that the output signal z(t) = 10x(t), the maximum value of W (in Hz) should be strictly less than ________.
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{array}{l} \quad x(t)=m(t) \cos 2400 \pi t \\ \text { thus } \quad y(t)=10 x(t)+x^{2}(t) \\ \therefore y(t)=10 m(t) \cos (2400 \pi t)+m^{2}(t) \cos ^{2}(2400 \pi t) \\ =10 m(t) \cos (2400 \pi t)+\frac{1}{2} m^{2}(t) \frac{1}{2} \cos (4800 \pi t) \end{array}[/latex]
Drawing the spectrum set spectrum of x(t) be



[latex]y(t) = 10x(t) + x^{2}(t)[/latex]


To recover z(t)
[latex] \begin{aligned} 1200-W \gt 700 & \Rightarrow W \lt 500 \\ 1200+W \lt 1700 & \Rightarrow W \lt 500 \\ 2 W \lt 700 & \Rightarrow W \lt 350 \\ 2400-2 W \gt 1700 & \Rightarrow W \lt 350 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: In a double side-band (DSB) full carrier AM transmission system, if the modulation index is doubled, then the ratio of total sideband power to the carrier power increases by a factor of ______.
questions.solution:
Ratio of [latex]P_{S B}[/latex] to [latex]P_{C}[/latex] is
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \quad P_{S B}={P}_{C}{\mu}^{2} \\ \begin{array}{l} \therefore \quad \frac{P_{S B}}{P_{C}}=\frac{\mu^{2}}{2} \\ \text { and }\left(\frac{P_{S B}}{P_{C}}\right)_{1}=\frac{\mu_{1}^{2}}{2} \\ \left(\frac{P_{S B}}{P_{C}}\right)_{2}=\frac{\mu_{2}^{2}}{2} \\ \text { where, } \quad\left(\frac{P_{S B}}{P_{C}}\right)_{2}=\frac{\mu_{2}^{2}}{2} \\ \text { hence } \frac{\left(P_{S B} / P_{C}\right)_{1}}{\left(P_{S B} / P_{C}\right)_{2}}=\frac{1}{4} \\ \left(\frac{P_{S B}}{P_{C}}\right)_{2}=4\left(\frac{P_{S B}}{P_{C}}\right)_{1} \end{array} \end{array}[/latex]
Four times.

[latex] =\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 402 \pi t+\sin 399 \pi t-\sin 398 \pi t) [/latex]
[latex] \quad+\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t+\sin 2 \pi t-\sin \pi t) [/latex]
After passing [latex]\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 402 \pi t+\sin 399 \pi t-\sin 398 \pi t) [/latex] term through LPF with cut-off frequency of 1 Hz , it results in a component of [latex]\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t)[/latex] at the output.

[latex] \begin{aligned} y(t) &=\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t)+\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t+\sin 2 \pi t-\sin \pi t) \\ &=\frac{\sin 2 \pi t}{t}+\frac{1}{2 t}(2 \sin 0.5 \pi t \cos 1.5 \pi t) \\ y(t) &=\frac{\sin 2 \pi t}{t}+\frac{\sin 0.5 \pi t}{t} \cos 1.5 \pi t \end{aligned}[/latex]

Consider a discrete memoryless source with an alphabet of four source symbols. [latex]s(t)[/latex] is a multi-level [latex](-1, 0, +1, +2)[/latex] signal representing a long sequence of random symbols from the above source which is generating [latex]10^4[/latex] symbols per second.

questions.solution:
Given:
4-level signal, symbol rate [latex]= 10^4[/latex] symbols/second.

Step 1: Nyquist bandwidth

The minimum (Nyquist) bandwidth required to transmit [latex]R_s[/latex] symbols/second without ISI is:

questions.text: A digital communication system transmits through a noiseless bandlimited channel [latex][-W W][/latex]. The received signal [latex]z(t)[/latex] at the output of the receiving filter is given by [latex]z(t)=\sum_{n} b[n] x(t-n T)[/latex] where [latex]b[n][/latex] are the symbols and [latex]x(t)[/latex] is the overall system response to a single symbol. The received signal is sampled at [latex]t=m T[/latex]. The Fourier transform of [latex]x(t)[/latex] is [latex]X(f)[/latex]. The Nyquist condition that [latex]X(f)[/latex] must satisfy for zero intersymbol interference at the receiver is ______
questions.solution:
For zero ISI, [latex]x(t)[/latex] should have zero crossings at [latex]\pm T, \pm 2 T, \pm 3 T \ldots[/latex]


[latex]x(t) \sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty} \delta(t-m T)=x(0) \delta(t)[/latex]
[latex]\frac{1}{T} \sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty} x\left(f-\frac{m}{T}\right)=x(0)[/latex]
[latex] \sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty} X\left(f-\frac{m}{T}\right)=x(0) T [/latex]
(or)
[latex] \sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty} X\left(f+\frac{m}{T}\right)=x(0) T [/latex]
As per GATE official Answer Key-MTA

questions.text:
Consider a channel over which either symbol [latex] x_A [/latex] or symbol [latex] x_B [/latex] is transmitted. Let the output of the channel Y be the input to a maximum likelihood (ML) detector at the receiver. The conditional probability density functions for Y given [latex] x_A [/latex]and [latex] x_B [/latex] are:

[latex] f_{Y|x_A}(y)=e^{-(y+1)}u(y+1), [/latex]
[latex] f_{Y|x_B}(y)=e^{(y-1)}(1-u(y-1)), [/latex]

where [latex] u(\cdot ) [/latex] is the standard unit step function. The probability of symbol error for this system is _________ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
ML decoding [latex] \rightarrow \; f_{Y/X_A}(y)\underset{\overset{ \lt }{X_B}}{\overset{X_A}{ \gt }} f_{Y/X_B}(y)[/latex]
[latex]i.e. \;\; f_{Y/X_A}(y) \gt f_{Y/X_B}(y) \rightarrow \text{ Decision favor of }X_A[/latex]
[latex]i.e. \;\; f_{Y/X_A}(y) \lt f_{Y/X_B}(y) \rightarrow \text{ Decision favor of }X_B[/latex]
For [latex]-1 \lt y \lt 0 [/latex] and [latex] 1 \lt y \lt \infty \rightarrow f_{Y/X_A}(y) \gt f_{Y/X_B}(y)[/latex]
For above internal decision in favor of [latex]X_A [/latex]
For [latex]-\infty \lt y \lt -1 [/latex] and [latex] 0\lt y \lt 1 \rightarrow f_{Y/X_B}(y) \gt f_{Y/X_A}(y)[/latex]
For above internal decision in favor of [latex]X_B [/latex]
[latex]P_e=P(X_A)\cdot P_{eX_A}+P(X_B)\cdot P_{eX_A} [/latex]
[latex] P_{eX_A}\rightarrow[/latex] Probability of error [latex] X_A[/latex] transmitted
[latex] P_{eX_B}\rightarrow[/latex] Probability of error [latex] X_B[/latex] transmitted
[latex]P_{eX_A}=\int_{0}^{1} f_{Y/X_A}(y)dy=\int_{0}^{1}e^{-(y+1)}u(y+1)dy= \int_{0}^{1}e^{-(y+1)} dy=e^{-1}-e^{-2}=0.23[/latex]
[latex]P_{eX_B}=\int_{0}^{1} f_{Y/X_B}(y)dy=\int_{0}^{1}e^{(y-1)} [1-u(y-1)]dy= \int_{0}^{1}e^{(y-1)} dy=e^{-1}-e^{-2}=0.23[/latex]
[latex] P_e=P(X_A) \times 0.23+P(X_B) \times 0.23 =0.23[P(X_A)+P(X_B)]=0.23 [/latex]

questions.text: A symbol stream contains alternate QPSK and 16-QAM symbols. If symbols from this stream are transmitted at the rate of 1 mega-symbols per second, the raw (uncoded) data rate is _______ mega-bits per second (rounded off to one decimal place).
questions.solution: [latex] \begin{aligned} \text{BIT RATE}&=[\text{SYBOL RATE}] \times \log_{20}M\\ 1.\;\; QPSK, \; M&=4,n=2\\ R_{b1}&=1 \times 2 =2mbps\\ 2.\;\; 16 QAM_1\Rightarrow  M=16,n=4\\ R_{b2}&=1 \times 4=4mbps\\ R_b&=\frac{2m+4m}{2}\\ R_b&=3 mbps \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: Let [latex]H(X)[/latex] denote the entropy of a discrete random variable [latex]X[/latex] taking [latex]K[/latex] possible distinct real values. Which of the following statements is/are necessarily true?
questions.solution:
[latex] H(X^2)=H(Y)=\Sigma P_Y(Y_i) \log _2 \frac{1}{P_Y(Y_i)}= \frac{1}{2} \log _2 2+\frac{1}{2} \log _2 2=1 bit/symbol[/latex]
[latex] H(X)=\frac{1}{4} \log _2 4+\frac{1}{2} \log _2 2+\frac{1}{4} \log _2 4=1.5 bit/symbol[/latex]
[latex]H(X) \gt H(X^2) [/latex]
Hence option (C) is not correct.

questions.text: A message signal having peak-to-peak value of [latex]2\:V[/latex], root mean square value of [latex]0.1\:V[/latex]  and bandwidth of [latex]\text{5 kHz}[/latex]  is sampled and fed to a pulse code modulation [latex](\text{PCM})[/latex]  system that uses a uniform quantizer. The [latex]\text{PCM}[/latex]  output is transmitted over a channel that can support a maximum transmission rate of [latex]\text{50 kbps}[/latex]. Assuming that the quantization error is uniformly distributed, the maximum signal to quantization noise ratio that can be obtained by the [latex]\text{PCM}[/latex] system (rounded off to two decimal places) is  ______
questions.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} v_{p-p} &=2 \mathrm{~V} \\ \text { Root MSQ }[m(t)] &=0.1 \mathrm{~V} ; \quad f_{m}=5 \mathrm{kHz} \\ \text { Channel capacity, } \quad C &=50 \mathrm{kbps} \\ \text{Max} \frac{S}{N_{Q}}=?\\ & \text{Signal power},\\ S&=\text{MSQ}[m(t)]=(0.1)^{2}=0.01\\ C &\geq R_{b} \Rightarrow 50 \mathrm{kbps} \geq n f_{s}\\ \because \qquad f_{s}&=N R=2 f_{m}=10 \mathrm{kHz}\\ n &\leq 5 \Rightarrow n_{\max }=5\\ N_{Q} &=\frac{\Delta^{2}}{12} \\ \therefore\qquad \Delta &=\frac{V_{p-p}}{2^{n}} \\ \Delta_{\min } &=\frac{V_{p-p}}{2^{7} \max }=\frac{2 V}{2^{5}}=\frac{1}{16} \\ \left(N_{Q}\right)_{\min } &=\frac{\Delta_{\min }^{2}}{12}=3.25 \times 10^{-4} \\ \left(\frac{S}{N Q}\right)_{\max } &=\frac{S}{\left(N_{Q}\right)_{\min }}=\frac{0.01}{3.25 \times 10^{-4}}=30.72 \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex] \begin{array}{c} f_{Y}(y \mid+1) P(+1) \sum_{-1}^{+1} f_{Y}(y \mid-1) F(-1) \\ P(+1)=0.80 \text { and } P(-1)=0.20 \end{array}[/latex]


[latex]P_{\theta(m \text { in })}=[/latex] Shaded area [latex]=2 \times \frac{1}{20}=0.10[/latex]

questions.text: A voice signal m(t) is in the frequency range 5 kHz to 15 kHz. The signal is amplitude-modulated to generate an AM signal [latex]f(t)=A(1+m(t))cos 2\pi f_c t[/latex], where [latex]f_c[/latex]=600kHz. The AM signal f(t) is to be digitized and archived. This is done by first sampling f(t) at 1.2 times the Nyquist frequency, and then quantizing each sample using a 256-level quantizer. Finally, each quantized sample is binary coded using K bits, where K is the minimum number of bits required for the encoding. The rate, in Megabits per second (rounded off to 2 decimal places), of the resulting stream of coded bits is _______ Mbps.
questions.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text { Nyquist rate } &=2 \times 615 \mathrm{kHz} \\ &=1230 \mathrm{kHz}=1.23 \mathrm{MHz} \\ f_{s} &=1.2 \times 1.23=1.476 \mathrm{MHz} \\ \text { Bits/sample }, n &=\log _{2}(256)=8 \\ \text { So, } \quad A_{D} &=n f_{s}=8 \times 1.476 \\ &=11.808 \simeq 11.81 \mathrm{Mbps} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text:
A single bit, equally likely to be 0 and 1, is to be sent across an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel with power spectral density [latex]N_0/2[/latex]. Binary signaling, with [latex]0\rightarrow p(t)[/latex] and [latex]1\rightarrow q(t)[/latex], is used for the transmission, along with an optimal receiver that minimizes the bit-error probability.

Let [latex]\varphi _1(t),\varphi _2(t)[/latex] form an orthonormal signal set.
If we choose [latex]p(t)=\varphi _1(t)\; and \; q(t)=-\varphi _2(t)[/latex], we would obtain a certain bit-error probability [latex]P_b[/latex].
If we keep [latex]p(t)=\varphi _1(t)[/latex], but take [latex]q(t)=\sqrt{E}\varphi _2(t)[/latex], for what value of E would we obtain the same bit-error probability [latex]P_b[/latex]?
questions.solution:
[latex]\text { When } p(t)=\phi_{1}(t) \text { and } q(t)=-\phi_{1}(t) [/latex]


[latex] d_{\min }=2[/latex]
[latex] \text { When } p(t)=\phi_{1}(t) \text { and } q(t)=-\sqrt{E}\phi_{2}(t)[/latex]
[latex] d_{\min }=\sqrt{(\sqrt{E})^{2}+1}=\sqrt{E+1}[/latex]


To obtain same bit-error probability, [latex]\sigma_{\text {min }} [/latex] should be same.
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text { So, } \quad \sqrt{E+1} &=2 \\ E &=3 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text:
A random variable X takes values -0.5 and 0.5 with probabilities 1/4 and 3/4, respectively. The noisy observation of X is Y = X + Z, where Z has uniform probability density over the interval (-1, 1). X and Z are independent. If the MAP rule based detector outputs [latex]\hat{X}[/latex] as

[latex]\hat{X}=\left\{\begin{matrix} -0.5 \; \; \; Y \lt \alpha \\ 0.5 \; \; \; Y \geq \alpha \end{matrix}\right.[/latex]

then the value of [latex]\alpha [/latex] (accurate to two decimal places) is _______.
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{array}{c} P\left(x_{0}\right)=\frac{1}{4} ; P\left(x_{1}\right)=\frac{3}{4} \\ \text { MAP criteria, } f_{Y}\left(y \mid x_{0}\right) P\left(x_{0}\right) \overset{x_{2}}{\underset{x_{1}}{\gtrless}}\left(y \mid x_{1}\right) P\left(x_{1}\right) \end{array}[/latex]


[latex]\text{So}\quad \alpha=-0.5[/latex]

questions.text:
A binary source generates symbols [latex] X \in \{-1,1\} [/latex]which are transmitted over a noisy channel. The probability of transmitting X= 1 is 0.5. Input to the threshold detector is R= X + N. The probability density function [latex]f_{N}(n)[/latex] of the noise N is shown below.
If the detection threshold is zero, then the probability of error (correct to two decimal places) is __________.
questions.solution:
Let [latex]s_{0}[/latex] and [latex]s_{1}[/latex] be the transmitted symbols representing the transmitted value {-1 , 1} respectively and let [latex]r_{0}[/latex] and [latex]r_{1}[/latex] be the received symbols.

Probability of error,
[latex] \begin{aligned} P_{e} &=P\left(s_{1}\right) P\left(r_{0} \mid s_{1}\right)+P\left(s_{0}\right) P\left(r_{1} \mid s_{0}\right) \\ P\left(r_{0} \mid s_{1}\right) &=P\left(r_{1} \mid s_{0}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{8}\\ \text{Given that,}\\ P\left(s_{0}\right)&=P\left(s_{1}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\\ \text{So}\quad P_{e}&=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{8}\right)=\frac{1}{8}=0.125 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: A sinusoidal message signal is converted to a PCM signal using a uniform quantizer. The required signal-to-quantization noise ratio (SQNR) at the output of the quantizer is 40dB. The minimum number of bits per sample needed to achieve the desired SQNR is _______

For sinusoidal input is applied to a PCM system,
[latex] \mathrm{SQNR}=6 n+1.8[/latex]
n= number of bits per sample
Given that, the required [latex]\mathrm{SQNR}=40 \mathrm{dB} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \mathrm{so}, 6 n+1.8 &\geq 40 \\ n &\geq \frac{38.2}{6}\\ n_{\min }&=7 \\ \because \; &n \text{ is always an integer value} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text:
In binary frequency shift keying (FSK), the given signal waveform are

[latex]u_{0}(t)=5cos(20000\pi t);o\leq t\leq T[/latex] , and
[latex]u_{1}(t)=5cos(22000\pi t);o\leq t\leq T[/latex],

Where T is the bit-duration interval and t is in seconds. Both [latex]u_{0}(t)[/latex] and [latex]u_{1}(t)[/latex] are zero outside the interval [latex]0\leq t \leq T[/latex]. With a matched filter (correlator) based receiver, the smallest positive value of T (in milliseconds) required to have [latex]u_{0}(t)[/latex] and [latex]u_{1}(t)[/latex] uncorrelated is
questions.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} u_{0}(t) &=5 \cos 20000 \pi t \\ u_{1}(t) &=5 \cos 22000 \pi t \\ f_{1} &=11000 \mathrm{Hz} \text { and } f_{2}=10000 \mathrm{Hz} \end{aligned}[/latex]
For FSK waveforms to be uncorrelated,
[latex] \begin{aligned} f_{1}-f_{2} &=n \frac{R_{b}}{2} ; n=1,2,3, \ldots \\ R_{b} &=\frac{2\left(f_{1}-f_{2}\right)}{n}=\frac{2000}{n}-\text { bits } / \mathrm{sec} \\ R_{b(\max )} &=2000 \mathrm{bits} / \mathrm{sec}\\ &\quad \quad \because \text{minimum value of n=1 }\\ T_{b(\min )}&=\frac{1}{R_{b(\max )}}=0.5 \mathrm{ms} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: Which one of the following statements about differential pulse code modulation (DPCM) is true?

questions.text: In a digital communication system, the overall pulse shape p(t) at the receiver before the sampler has the Fourier transform P(f). If the symbols are transmitted at the rate of 2000 symbols per second, for which of the following cases is inter symbol interference zero?

Given,
Symbol rate =2000 symbol/sec
So [latex]R_{b}=2 \mathrm{kHz}[/latex]

[latex] \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} P\left(f-n R_{b}\right)=\text { Constant }[/latex]

questions.text: The bit error probability of a memoryless binary symmetric channel is [latex]10^{-5}[/latex]. If [latex]10^{5}[/latex] bits are sent over this channel, then the probability that not more than one bit will be in error is __________
questions.solution:
bit error probability, [latex]p=10^{-5} [/latex]
Number of bits transmitted,
[latex] n=10^{5}[/latex]
If n-bits are transmitted, probability of getting error in 'r' bits is given by
[latex] p_{e}={ }^{n} C_{r} \rho^{r}(1-p)^{n-r}[/latex]
The probability that not more than one bit will be in error is
[latex] \begin{array}{l} ={ }^{n} C_{0} p^{0}(1-p)^{-0}+{ }^{n} C_{\{(p)}^{1}(1-p)^{p-1} \\ =(1-p)^{n}+n p(1-p)^{n-1} \\ =\left(1-10^{-5}\right)^{10^{5}}+10^{5} \times 10^{-5}\left(1-10^{-5}\right)^{10^{5}-1} \\ =0.7357 \end{array}[/latex]

questions.text: An ideal band-pass channel 500Hz - 2000Hz is deployed for communication. A modem is designed to transmit bits at the rate of 4800 bits/s using 16-QAM. The roll-off factor of a pulse with a raised cosine spectrum that utilizes the entire frequency band is ________
questions.solution: [latex]\begin{array}{l} \text { Channel spectrum } 500 \mathrm{Hz}-2000 \mathrm{Hz} \\ \text { hence } B W=1500 \mathrm{Hz} \\ B W=\frac{R_{b}}{\log _{2} M}(1+\alpha) \\ 1500=\frac{R_{b}}{\log _{2} 16}(1+\alpha) \\ 1500=\frac{4800}{\log _{2} 16}(1+\alpha) \\ 1500=1200(1+\alpha) \\ \Rightarrow \quad \alpha=0.25 \end{array}[/latex]

questions.text: A speech signal is sampled at 8 kHz and encoded into PCM format using 8 bits/sample. The PCM data is transmitted through a baseband channel via 4-level PAM. The minimum bandwidth (in kHz) required for transmission is _______
questions.solution: [latex]\begin{array}{l} f_{s}=8 \mathrm{kHz} \\ n=8 \text { bits/sample } \\ M=4 \\ B W_{\min }=\frac{R_{b}}{2 \log _{2} M}=\frac{R_{b}}{4}=\frac{8 \times 8}{4}=16 \mathrm{kHz} \end{array}[/latex]

questions.text: An analog pulse s(t) is transmitted over an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel. The received signal is r(t) = s(t) + n(t), where n(t) is additive white Gaussian noise with power spectral density [latex]\frac{N_{0}}{2}[/latex]. The received signal is passed through a filter with impulse response h(t). Let [latex]E_{s}[/latex] and [latex]E_{h}[/latex] denote the energies of the pulse s(t) and the filter h(t), respectively. When the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is maximized at the output of the filter ([latex]SNR_{max}[/latex]), which of the following holds?

When the signal to Noise ratio is maximum
[latex] h(t)=s(T-t)[/latex]
but shifting doesn't change the energy
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad E_{h}&=E_{s} \\ \text{and(SNR)}_{\max }&=\frac{2 E_{s}}{N_{0}} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.text: Consider binary data transmission at a rate of 56 kbps using baseband binary pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) that is designed to have a raised-cosine spectrum. The transmission bandwidth (in kHz) required for a roll-off factor of 0.25 is ________
questions.solution:
Bit rate, [latex] \quad R_{b}=56 \mathrm{kbps} [/latex]

questions.text:
A source emits bit 0 with probability 1/3 and bit 1 with probability 2/3. The emitted bits are communicated to the receiver. The receiver decides for either 0 or 1 based on the received value R . It is given that the conditional density functions of R are as
[latex]f_{(R|0)}(r)=\left\{\begin{matrix} \frac{1}{4}, & -3\leq x\leq 1,\\ 0, & otherwise, \end{matrix}\right. [/latex] and

[latex]f_{(R|1)}(r)=\left\{\begin{matrix} \frac{1}{6}, &-1\leq x\leq 5, \\ 0,& otherwise. \end{matrix}\right.[/latex]
The minimum decision error probability is
questions.solution:
According to MAP criteria, for optimum threshold,
[latex] f_{R}\left(r \mid s_{0}\right) P\left(s_{0}\right) \sum_{k_{1}}^{r_{0}} f_{B}\left(r \mid s_{1}\right) P\left(s_{1}\right)[/latex]
Given that,
[latex] P\left(s_{0}\right)=\frac{1}{3} \text { and } P\left(s_{1}\right)=\frac{2}{3}[/latex]


From the above figure, it is clear that,
[latex] \begin{array}{l} f_{B}\left(r \mid s_{0}\right) P\left(s_{0}\right)>f_{R}\left(r \mid s_{1}\right) P\left(s_{1}\right) \Rightarrow \text { for } r<-1 \\ f_{A}\left(r \mid s_{1}\right) P\left(s_{1}\right)>f_{R}\left(r \mid s_{0}\right) P\left(s_{0}\right) \Rightarrow \text { for } r>-1 \end{array}[/latex]
So, optimum threshold will be, [latex]r_{\mathrm{th}}=-1 [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text{ For }r_{\mathrm{th}}=-1& \\ P\left(r_{0} \mid s_{1}\right) P\left(s_{1}\right)&=0\\ P\left(r_{1} \mid s_{0}\right) P\left(s_{0}\right)&=\frac{1}{12}[1-(-1)]=\frac{1}{6} \\ P_{e(\mathrm{min})}&=P\left(r_{0} \mid s_{1}\right) P\left(s_{1}\right)+P\left(q \mid s_{0}\right) P\left(s_{0}\right)=\frac{1}{6} \end{aligned}[/latex]
